analyst_view.overall: Betis are 4th with 27 points and unbeaten in four league games, the last a 1-1 derby draw with Sevilla, while Rayo are 16th with 12 points and lost 0-1 at home to Valencia last weekend. Betis played a Champions League game in Bratislava on Tuesday and host Rayo at 14:00 on Saturday, a short turnaround the numbers do not see; Bellerín, Natan and Bartra were rested for the first half there. Ceballos (muscle) and Lo Celso (knee) were still not training with the group on Thursday and are doubtful, and one report says Abde also missed Thursday's session for an unexplained reason; none of the three is in the numbers, while Morante, whom the numbers count as out, is back in group training. Rayo, under Beñat San José, still miss Batalla and Luiz Felipe (counted), and Óscar Valentín trained with the group for the first time but awaits medical clearance. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and take only about 3% off Betis for Morante, who is in fact back in group training. Ceballos and Lo Celso are still training apart and doubtful, and one report says Abde, one of Betis's main attacking threats, skipped Thursday's training; the numbers know none of this, and Betis also come off a Tuesday Champions League trip. I trim to about 2.3, mostly on Betis's side; small because Morante's return partly offsets it and Abde's problem is not confirmed.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Betis's recent rise in corners (33 in six) already added. Betis attack wide and Rayo push their full-backs on, with Pedrosa expected back at left-back; if Abde misses out, Ruibal or Antony would still play wide, so the pattern should hold. I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, with Rayo expected to take most of them; both sides' recent card counts and the past meetings are already counted. The referee has not been named yet, so his record can't be judged, and I found no suspension or tension issue beyond what the numbers know. I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.0 shots, pushed up by strong recent shot counts on both sides (Rayo 104 in their last six), which they already add. Betis played in Bratislava on Tuesday night and kick off at 14:00 on Saturday, with Ceballos and Lo Celso doubtful and Abde a new question mark, so some rotation and a lower Betis output are likely. I trim to about 29.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, with both sides' recent accuracy already counted. Betis may be without their two main creators, Ceballos and Lo Celso, and possibly Abde, after a midweek European trip, which the numbers don't see; Rayo's weak finishing away is already in. I trim slightly to about 9.1.
